claim: Census of India 2011 counted 199,812,341 people in Uttar Pradesh.

evidence.locator: A-01, state row 09 UTTAR PRADESH, Total (xlsx row 2525; extract in method/census_a01_extract_output.txt)
Appendix 1, Table 1 (PDF page 28), row Uttar Pradesh

notes: Final census count (1 March 2011 reference). A provisional figure of 199,581,477 exists in older tables; the final A-01 figure is used. Say 'about 200 million' or '19.98 crore'.

claim: Uttar Pradesh has an area of 240,928 sq km (Census 2011 basis).

evidence.locator: A-01, state row 09 UTTAR PRADESH, Total
Table 3.5.3 row 27 (source line: India State of Forest Report 2009)

method: Our own cross-check: Natural Earth polygon area = 240,677 sq km (C022).
notes: Total geographical area as recorded by the Census. Survey of India's own state area table was not opened (see open_questions.md).

claim: Census 2011 population density of Uttar Pradesh: 829 per sq km (199,812,341 / 240,928 = 829.3).

evidence.locator: A-01, state row 09 UTTAR PRADESH, Total

claim: Uttar Pradesh holds 16.50% of India's 2011 population (1 in 6): 199,812,341 of 1,210,854,977.

evidence.locator: A-01 rows INDIA Total (xlsx row 5) and UTTAR PRADESH (row 2525)

method: 199,812,341 / 1,210,854,977 = 0.16502 (python, method/census_a01_extract.py then arithmetic in sources check)
notes: Both the Census count and NCP's own share column give 16.50%.

claim: Uttar Pradesh is 7.33% of India's area: 240,928 of 3,287,469 sq km (Census A-01 areas).

evidence.locator: A-01 rows INDIA Total and UTTAR PRADESH Total

notes: Census A-01 India area 3,287,469 includes areas India administers and claims (footnote marks '@&' on the INDIA row); the Technical Group tables elsewhere use 3,287,263 (MoSPI/FSI table total 3,287,263). Differences are 0.006%. Use '7%' or 'about one-fourteenth'.

claim: The government's Technical Group on Population Projections (Nov 2019, National Commission on Population) projects 243,466 thousand people (about 24.3 crore) in Uttar Pradesh on 1 July 2026.

evidence.locator: Appendix 2, Table 11 (Projected Total Population by Sex as on 1st July), UP column, PDF page 88; row 2026

notes: A projection, not a count. India's total is 14,26,907 thousand on the same table (PDF page 86). The projection starts from the 2011 census and assumes 2001-2011 migration persists; the next real count is the 2027 census (C019). Say 'projected' or 'an official estimate'.

claim: The same Table 11 gives Uttar Pradesh 200,897 thousand on 1 July 2011 and 259,459 thousand on 1 July 2036.

evidence.locator: Table 11, UP column, PDF page 88; rows 2011 and 2036

claim: On a one-year, one-basis comparison for 1 July 2026, with UP's NCP projection (243.5 million) set against the UN's WPP 2024 medium estimates for 237 countries and areas, Uttar Pradesh would rank sixth in the world by population: behind China, the rest of India, the United States, Indonesia and Pakistan; ahead of Nigeria and Brazil.
method: method/rank_population.py: WPP2024 Medium, Time=2026, LocTypeName='Country/Area' (237); UP inserted at 243,466 thousand; 'the rest of India' counted as a separate country, as the pitch requires.
notes: Robust to basis: scaling UP's NCP share of India (17.06%) onto the UN's own India figure gives 251.9 million, still sixth (C011).

claim: In 2026 the countries immediately around UP are Pakistan at 259.3 million (above), Nigeria at 242.4 million (below, 1.0 million or 0.4% fewer than UP) and Brazil at 213.6 million (UP has 29.9 million, 14%, more).
method: WPP2024 Medium, 1 July 2026, thousands; differences in method/derived_output.txt
notes: UP-Nigeria is a near tie on the direct basis (0.4%); on the scaled basis (C011) UP leads Nigeria by 4%. Hedge: 'about level with Nigeria'.

claim: On the 2011 census count (199.8 million) set against WPP 2024's 2011 estimates, UP ranks sixth, not fifth: Pakistan's estimate (203.7 million) is above it and Brazil's (195.3 million) is below.

evidence.quote: countries just above UP: [('United States of America', 314105), ('Indonesia', 249470), ('Pakistan', 203746)]

notes: Basis-sensitive: the UN's 2011 figure for India (1,261,225 thousand) is 4.2% above the census count (1,210,855 thousand). Scaling UP up to the UN's India gives 208.1 million, which would be fifth (C011, conflicts.md K1). So 2011 is 'fifth or sixth depending on basis'; 2026 is sixth on both.

claim: If UP's share of India (16.50% in 2011; 17.06% on the 2026 projection) is applied to the UN's own India figures, UP would be 208.1 million in 2011 (fifth, above Pakistan) and 251.9 million in 2026 (sixth, below Pakistan 259.3, above Nigeria 242.4).

evidence.quote: 2026: UN India 1,476,626k x UP share 0.1706 = 251,949k -> rank 6 of 238
2011: UN India 1,261,225k x UP share 0.1650 = 208,124k -> rank 5 of 238

claim: By area, UP (240,928 sq km) is not a large country: it would rank about 81st of 216 countries on FAO/World Bank surface area (2021), just below Uganda (241,550) and the United Kingdom (243,610) and just above Ghana (238,533).
method: method/rank_area.py: 215 WPP 'Country/Area' locations with an ISO3 code and a WDI value; UP at 240,928
notes: Basis difference: WDI surface area includes inland water; Census 'area' is total geographical area. UP versus UK/Uganda differs by 0.3-1.1%, so say 'about the size of the United Kingdom', not 'bigger' or 'smaller'. Our own Natural Earth check (C022): UK 242,737, UP 240,677.

claim: UP's area is within about 1% of the United Kingdom's (240,928 vs 243,610 sq km, WDI/FAO; 240,677 vs 242,737 on our Natural Earth measure).
method: method/area_ne.py (spherical area on the authalic sphere; holes subtracted)

claim: In 2026 Uttar Pradesh has about 3.5 times the people of the United Kingdom (243.5 vs 69.9 million) on about the same area.
Nigeria's area is about 3.8 times UP's, Pakistan's 3.3 times, Brazil's 35 times (FAO/World Bank surface area 2021; our Natural Earth measure gives 3.8, 3.3 and 35.3).
method: method/derived.py (WDI ratios to 240,928); Natural Earth ratios computed from method/area_ne_output.json (Nigeria 911,216 / 240,677 = 3.79; Pakistan 796,732 = 3.31; Brazil 8,504,678 = 35.3)

claim: On the 2026 projection UP has about 1,010 people per sq km, denser than every country in WPP 2024 with more than 10 million people except Bangladesh (1,205).

evidence.quote: countries >10M people 2026 with density above UP: [('Bangladesh', 1205)]

method: method/derived.py: WPP2024 2026 population / WDI 2021 surface area; UP = 243,466,000 / 240,928
notes: Mixed years and area bases (projection / 2011 geographical area), so hedge: 'around a thousand per square kilometre'. Not spine.

claim: The nearest sea coast to any point of UP's boundary is about 480 km away (Odisha coast), so UP is landlocked.

evidence.quote: min distance UP vertex -> India sea-coast vertex: 479 km

method: method/landlocked_check.py: coast = vertices of India's admin-0 outline (India point of view) not within 0.03 deg of another country's vertex; UP vertices from admin-1; haversine minimum over all pairs.
notes: Approximate: Natural Earth 1:10m vertices, not Survey of India; say 'nearly 500 km from the sea' or 'at least 450 km'. No official 'landlocked' statement was opened.

claim: UNCTAD's list of 32 landlocked developing countries ('informally accepted by UN member States on geographical grounds') has Ethiopia as its most populous member at 138.9 million in 2026 (WPP 2024); UP's 243.5 million is 1.75 times that.

evidence.quote: Of which, 17 are Landlocked Least Developed Countries
List informally accepted by UN member States on geographical grounds.

method: method/derived.py: 32 names from S09 matched to WPP locations (no unmatched)
notes: The list covers developing countries only. Landlocked countries not on it (for example Czechia, Austria, Switzerland, Hungary, Serbia) are all under 11 million in WPP 2026 (derived_output.txt); we did not open a source listing every landlocked country, so say 'bigger than any country on the UN's landlocked list'.

claim: The next census of India has a reference date of 1 March 2027 (population enumeration in February 2027); the last census was in 2011, so every population figure for 2026 is a projection.

evidence.locator: slide 'Reference Date and Phases of Census 2027'

notes: Says 'February, 2027' for Population Enumeration. Date of the deck: 30 April 2026.

claim: The Technical Group's projections were prepared for use by the National Commission on Population, NITI Aayog and other stakeholders, as a revision of the 'existing official projection figures'.

evidence.quote: to revise the existing official projection figures
it had been decided to constitute a Technical Group on Population Projections

notes: Defines why we may call the 2026 figure 'an official projection'. Its author is the government's own demographic panel.

claim: The UN's WPP 2024 puts India at 1,261,225 thousand in 2011 against the census count of 1,210,855 thousand (UN 4.2% higher), so UN country figures and Indian census figures are not on one basis.
notes: This is why we publish the rank on two bases (C010, C011).

evidence.quote: NE UP area = 240,677 km2 ; NE India area = 3,273,927 km2 ; UP share = 7.35%
